title: Fit the blue suction-cup tool to a robot's manual quick-change flange and lock it on
instruction: Fit the blue suction-cup tool to the robot's tool flange and lock it on, leaving the gripper tool in the rack. Then let go of everything, with the tool hanging locked on the robot, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Robot cells swap end effectors (grippers, suction cups, welding torches) on quick-change tool changers. When a technician changes a tool by hand, on a manual changer or while recovering a cell after a fault, the new tool has to be held up square against the robot's flange while a locking ring or lever is turned; let go too early and the tool drops, damaging it or the fixture. One hand holds the tool, the other works the lock.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A robot arm of cast aluminium, fixed (switched off), its base 56 cm forward and 11 cm left of the centre line; its wrist reaches in low, ending in a steel tool flange whose face (7 cm across), 2 cm left of the centre line, looks to the right; the flange's axis is 30 cm forward and 8.5 cm above the table. A light on top of the wrist shows red. (2) A steel locking ring 8.8 cm across and 1.8 cm deep turning on the flange just behind its face, with three claws reaching 1.1 cm in front of the face, and an orange-anodised aluminium lever reaching 11 cm toward the arms and then bending to the left to a black rubber pad 4.5 by 3 cm (its middle 19 cm forward, 8.3 cm left of the centre line, its top 9.9 cm above the table, with a small lip on its near end). Ring and lever weigh 661 g. Pressing the pad down turns the ring, up to 35 degrees (the pad then 6.6 cm lower); friction (0.12 N m) keeps it where it is left, and the lever's weight (0.07 N m) helps it down. (3) An aluminium tool rack right of the centre line with two slots, each tool lying along the left-right line, its plate facing left toward the flange: a blue suction-cup tool (120 g; an anodised-aluminium plate 6 cm across, its face 30 cm forward and 12 cm right of the centre line; a blue anodised-aluminium body 4.4 cm thick ending in a black nitrile-rubber suction cup 22.5 cm right of the centre line), and the robot's grey aluminium two-finger gripper tool (140 g), the same but 18 cm forward. Each tool has a square black acetal handle 1.6 cm across on top, 5 cm from its plate's face, its top 14 cm above the table. A tool is seated when its plate's face is within 6 mm of the flange's face, its middle within 6 mm of the flange's axis, its axis within 9 degrees of the flange's and it is turned within 8 degrees of handle-up: the range the changer's lead-ins guide a plate in from. A tool seated while the ring is within 8 degrees of open is locked on once the ring is turned 25 degrees: it is drawn square onto the flange and the light turns green. Turned back below 25 degrees it is no longer locked (the light turns red); back within 8 degrees of open it comes free. A ring turned with no tool seated locks nothing. The changer, a manual locking-ring type (the README's design tables give every size, fit and material; angles are seen facing the flange): the flange (a 70 mm lip in front of a 64 mm journal) is bolted to the wrist (ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6) by four M6 screws on a 50 mm circle, through a 76 mm retaining disc behind the ring. Two 6 mm dowels stand 6 mm out of its face, 22 mm from the axis at 12 o'clock (round) and 6 o'clock (diamond). The ring's 64 mm bore turns on the journal (H7/g6); a wave washer between the lip and the ring holds it back against the disc, and its friction keeps the ring where it is left; a 4 mm pin in the disc, running in a groove in the ring's back, stops it at 1 degree past open and at 35 degrees. The ring's three claws (at 2, 6 and 10 o'clock with the ring open, each 80 degrees of arc) have lips 32 to 38 mm from the axis whose back faces are cams: a lead-in ramp from 9.0 to 3.6 mm in front of the face (ring turned 8 to 20 degrees), a clamp ramp to 2.8 mm (20 to 25 degrees) and a flat dwell. Each tool plate (8 mm thick) has three lugs at 12, 4 and 8 o'clock, each 24 degrees wide, from its rim to 36 mm from the axis and 3 mm thick, and two bushed holes for the dowels. With the ring open the lugs pass through the 40-degree gaps between the lips; turned 25 degrees, the lips pull the plate onto the face with about 16 N. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 if the gripper tool was ever locked on. Otherwise 1.0: the suction tool locked on (seated with the ring open, then the ring turned 25 degrees or more, and still turned 25 degrees or more), each gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) at least 4 cm from its handle and from the lever's pad, and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the suction tool locked on otherwise; 0.25: the suction tool seated on the flange, with the ring open, at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the suction tool still. In a real trial, the same tiers are judged from the changer and the video: locked = at the end, the ring's index line is at or past the LOCK mark (25 degrees) on the retaining disc, a 0.1 mm feeler gauge does not enter between plate and face, and the tool hangs on the robot; seated with the ring open = the plate on both dowels while the index line was inside the 8-degree mark; the gripper tool locked = the same test for it, at any time; hands clear and arms home = TCP distances from the arms' logged joint angles, as in the simulation.
reset_notes: Turn the ring back open, take the suction tool off and lay both tools back in the rack.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) at real size and mass. Simplified: the robot is fixed; the claws, lugs and dowels are drawn but do not touch, so seating is a pose check over the lead-ins' range and the lock a fixed joint switched on at 25 degrees with a tool seated, holding it square until 8 degrees (a real one has play below 25); the washer's friction is a hinge spring moved to where the ring is left, without the clamp ramps' extra 0.2 N m. Cameras 1280 x 704.
